items.q: How do I set it up?
items.a: Sign in with gh auth login. In ScreenClip Settings, add your repository, base branch, and validation command, then connect a coding agent.

items.q: Can my coding agent check what’s open in ScreenClip?
items.a: In Settings › AI Agents, use “Check tasks from your agents” to let Codex or Claude Code see your report queue and close reports they fixed themselves.
Your agent may send the screenshot and note to its provider. Approved screenshots are committed to your GitHub repository. See the {link:privacy} for details on sharing and redaction.

items.q: Does a fix merge on its own?
items.a: Automatic merge is optional for each project. When enabled, the fix must pass validation, GitHub checks, and required reviews.

items.q: What if my crop is too tight?
items.a: Add another screenshot or note to the same report, even while the agent is working.
I’m {link:author}. I built ScreenClip to file bugs while testing my own apps. Feedback and pull requests are welcome on GitHub.

features: Region screenshots with a configurable global shortcut
Optional notes, drawing, arrows, shapes, text, and opaque redaction
Capture from websites and native Mac apps
Codex, Claude Code, and Grok Bot
Project validation, GitHub pull requests, optional merge, and a retest queue
Claude Code and Codex can read project reports, suggest settings for you to approve, and close reports they fixed
Reports from your own iPhone and iPad apps with ScreenClipKit, in Debug builds

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: ScreenClip stores reports on your Mac. Your coding agent may send them to its provider, and screenshots committed to GitHub are visible to everyone with access to the repository.
privacy.stays1: ScreenClip saves reports, screenshots, notes, annotations, settings, questions, and activity in {code:appSupport}. Reports use a SQLite database and separate image files. Local agents use Git worktrees in this folder, separate from your project checkout.
privacy.stays2: A diagnostics log in that folder records build and API error metadata. It does not include screenshots, notes, browser URLs, or window titles.
privacy.stays3: ScreenClip saves your Grok Bot webhook URL and Authorization header in the macOS Keychain under {code:keychain}. These credentials stay out of the queue database.
privacy.stays4: ScreenClip has no user accounts or report server. The app contains no analytics, ads, or crash reporter that sends data to ScreenClip.
privacy.stays5: Once a day, ScreenClip downloads its update feed from GitHub Releases, and a new version from there when one is available. GitHub receives ordinary connection data, such as IP address and a user agent with the app version. No system profile or usage data is sent. Automatic installation can be turned off in Settings → General → Updates.
privacy.capture1: ScreenClip uses Screen Recording permission to capture the region you select. It does not record continuously.
privacy.capture2: A capture can include the app name, bundle ID, and front window title for project matching and context. Enabling {ui:browserUrl} also allows ScreenClip to request Safari or Chrome automation and save the URL. With this setting off, ScreenClip never collects the URL.
privacy.redact1: Use the redact tool to replace private pixels with solid black. Other markup, including arrows, shapes, pen strokes, and text, leaves the pixels underneath intact.
privacy.redact2: ScreenClip discards the unredacted crop. Only the flattened image can go to an agent, GitHub, or a webhook.
privacy.local1: Codex and Claude Code receive the approved screenshot, note, and prompt on your Mac. ScreenClip also publishes report screenshots to the project’s GitHub repository with the fix.
privacy.local2: Each agent uses your account and may send the prompt and images to its provider under that account’s terms. Codex uses its app-server, and Claude Code uses its own login. ScreenClip starts them without GitHub tokens and handles pushes and pull requests itself.
privacy.local3: Installing ScreenClip’s local MCP server lets agent sessions read report titles, notes, statuses, questions, and activity. Agents can also suggest project settings for you to accept, and close reports they fixed themselves. The agent may send these details to its provider. The server sends nothing itself. Remove it from the agent to stop access.
privacy.github1: Pull request automation uses the GitHub CLI you install and the GitHub account that CLI is logged into. ScreenClip pushes a {code:branch} branch, and for Codex and Claude Code it opens the pull request. It reads check status, and it merges only when automatic merge is enabled for that project and the checks and review rules pass. It also lists the project’s merged pull requests to find any that name a report as “ScreenClip #N”, and moves those reports to To retest.
privacy.grok1: Nothing is sent to Grok Bot until you save a webhook URL and Authorization header. Once that connection is saved, every report you send to Grok Bot shares its approved screenshots. There is no separate sharing setting for a project, whether its repository is private or public.
privacy.grok3: Anyone who can read the repository can access the evidence; in a public repository, that includes anyone on the internet. Removing files from a later commit does not erase them from Git history. Grok Bot opens the pull request from that branch. Cancel stops the local record and, if the connection supports cancellation, sends a best-effort request; the remote run may still finish. Grok Bot questions stay in its chat.
privacy.grok4: A redirect of the webhook to a different host does not include the Authorization header.
privacy.delete1: Delete a report in ScreenClip to remove its local screenshots and notes. That does not delete the agent’s own conversation history, or a pull request already opened on GitHub. Removing the app does not by itself delete {code:appSupport} or the Keychain item.
privacy.delete2: GitHub, and the provider behind the agent you signed into, keep what they received under their own terms.
privacy.tips: Choosing a tip opens GitHub Sponsors in your browser. ScreenClip receives no payment, card, or payout details through the app. You can dismiss the tip prompt, turn it off, or reopen it from the menu or Settings. This website does not link to a payment page.
privacy.site2: Clicks on the download link are also counted, together with the part of the page the link was in. Nothing else about you is added to that count.
privacy.contact: Questions about this policy go through the {link:support}.
privacy.changes: Material changes to this policy will be posted on this page, with an updated date.
privacy.github2a: The pull request includes the agent’s summary, the report reference, and the validation command with secret-like values redacted.
privacy.github2b: For Codex and Claude Code, ScreenClip commits the annotated, redacted screenshots you approved and the agent’s retest screenshots. It embeds them in the pull request for comparison. It is on by default. Turn off “Commit screenshots to the repository” in a project’s settings to commit no screenshots; its pull requests then describe Before and After in words.
privacy.github2c: Everyone with repository access can see these images. In a public repository, anyone can see them. Deleting files in a later commit leaves them in Git history. ScreenClip never publishes the unredacted crop.
privacy.grok2a: ScreenClip then pushes the approved PNGs and a {code:reportJson} file to a {code:branch} branch in the project repository, and sends a small JSON webhook. The webhook does not contain image bytes.
privacy.grok2b: It includes the report number, issue id, revision, title, notes, later context notes, source app name, bundle ID, project name, repository, base branch, validation command, and the evidence branch, commit, and file paths. The browser URL and window title are included only when {ui:browserUrl} is on. The webhook also includes a workspace ID, previous pull request URLs, and delivery identifiers.
privacy.grok2c: The webhook and {code:reportJson} also carry ScreenClip’s instructions for the agent and your default prompt add-on from Settings. A supported cancel request sends the issue ID, report number, revision, repository, and branch.
privacy.site1a: {link:site} is a static website. Pages on this site load no scripts or fonts from other domains.
privacy.site1b: The site uses Vercel Web Analytics, provided by the host that serves it, to count visitors and page views. It sets no cookies. It records the page address, the referring site, the browser, operating system, and device type, and the country derived from the IP address. It does not store the IP address and does not follow you across other sites.
privacy.site1c: Choosing a language stores that choice in a cookie named screenclip_lang and in local storage on your device. The cookie only selects the language for the home page. It is not used for advertising or analytics. The host that serves the site receives ordinary connection data, such as IP address and user agent, in order to deliver the page.
privacy.ios1a: ScreenClipKit sends Debug reports directly to your paired Mac over the local network, encrypted for that Mac. Reports include the annotated screenshot, note, and device and app details. You can turn off recent app logs, screen layout, and device state. When diagnostics are enabled, the app can also attach its own text or JSON files. The agent can read those files with the report.
privacy.ios1b: Reports wait on your iPhone or iPad until the Mac is reachable. The Mac then stores them like other reports. Release builds omit the reporting code.

support.title: Support
support.statusReady: {link:download} gets the latest disk image from GitHub Releases. ScreenClip 1.2.1 is free for noncommercial use.
support.statusSoon: ScreenClip is coming soon. There is no download available yet.
support.issues: Report a bug or ask a question in {link:issues}. Include your macOS version, the agent you used, and what happened. Redact private details before sharing screenshots.
support.issuesMissing: Public support is not available yet.
support.needOs: A Mac with Apple silicon running macOS 14 or later.
support.needGit: A local Git repository. Add its website addresses or app bundle IDs and validation command in Settings.
support.needAgent: At least one agent: Codex CLI with {code:appServer}, Claude Code, or Grok Bot (a webhook URL and Authorization header).
support.needGh: GitHub CLI, signed in to the account you use for pull requests.
support.needRecord: Screen Recording permission, so ScreenClip can capture the region you select.
support.awake: Keep ScreenClip open and your Mac awake for Codex or Claude Code. Grok Bot works remotely. Its status updates when you reopen ScreenClip.
support.build: The README covers local signing and the ScreenClip scheme. Use Xcode 16 or later with Swift 6.
support.buildMissing: The source is not public yet.
support.capture: Choose {ui:checkAccess} in Settings. After granting access in System Settings, choose {ui:checkAgain} or {ui:reopen}. The README has the permission reset steps.
support.privacy: See the {link:privacy} for screenshot sharing, storage, and redaction.

flow.s1Body: Press ⌘⇧2 and drag over what you noticed, in any Mac app or website. On iPhone or iPad, shake the device.
flow.s2Body: Type a quick note. Mark it up or black out anything private if you want, then send.
flow.s3Body: Your coding agent picks up the report, makes the fix, and opens a pull request. Nothing to watch.
flow.s4Body: ScreenClip notifies you when the fix merges. Pull requests for visual fixes include before and after screenshots.

iosPage.title: Report bugs from iOS
iosPage.shotAlt: The ScreenClipKit report sheet over a demo app. A red box and an arrow mark a clipped Add to order button, and the note says the price is cut off.
iosPage.howTitle: Pair your device and send a report
iosPage.step1Body: Shake the device, or take a screenshot and tap Report. Mark the issue, redact private details, and tap Send. You can also choose a screenshot you took earlier.
iosPage.step2Body: Reports are encrypted for your paired Mac. If it’s offline, they wait on your iPhone or iPad and send when it reconnects.
iosPage.step4Body: When a fix merges, try it on your iPhone or iPad. Tap “Looks fixed” to close the report or “Still broken” to add another capture.
iosPage.pairBody: Connect both devices to the same network. On your Mac, open Settings › iOS, enable “Receive reports from iOS devices,” and click “Pair a device.” On your iPhone or iPad, shake, tap the gear, then Pair. Confirm the six-digit code on both screens.
iosPage.pairAlt: ScreenClip Settings › iOS on the Mac, asking to confirm the 6-digit code shown on the iPhone.
iosPage.setupIntro: You need ScreenClip 1.2.0 or later on your Mac, and an app for iOS 17 or later built with Xcode 16 or newer.
iosPage.setup1Body: In Xcode, choose File › Add Package Dependencies, enter this URL, and link ScreenClipKit to your app target.
iosPage.setup2Body: Call start once, from your App initializer or your app delegate.
iosPage.setup3Title: Allow the local network, in Debug only
iosPage.setup3Body: Add these two keys to the Info.plist of the Debug configuration, so the app can find your Mac.
iosPage.agentTip: For help with setup, open Settings › iOS on your Mac. Choose “Copy agent prompt” and paste it into Codex or Claude Code in your iOS project.
iosPage.releaseNote: Release and TestFlight builds use an empty stub. Keep the local network keys in your Debug configuration.
